title: TAPP Composition Module: ICPMS
description:
The shared ICPMS block of the 2026-08-11 TAPP library (Claude Skills for TAPP/Module_ICPMS.csv), composed by 9 of the sixteen delivery tables. 39 owned fields over 14 schema paths.

GENERATED by tools/build_module_bb.py from the module's CSV and its schema-path sidecar — edit those, not this file. Requiredness follows the TAPP tier matrix: a field Basic on a side is required there, Advanced is permitted, N/A is absent from that side entirely.

This is a PROFILE, not a vocabulary: it asserts which properties a conforming procedure or analysis carries. Column F (Example / Allowed Content) is consumer-owned per the module manifest, so no enum is pinned here — a consuming TAPP may narrow a value space, never widen it.

Instrument.title: ADA Analysis Instrument
Instrument.description: ADA analytical instrument building block. Extends the core CDIF instrument building block with NeXus NXinstrument classification via additionalType. Instruments are typed as schema:Thing + schema:Product (from core) with domain-specific types (e.g. nxs:base_classes/NXinstrument.html, ada:AMSInstrument) in additionalType.

allOf.title: Instrument Description
allOf.description: Schema for describing laboratory instruments and instrument systems. Supports ownership, manufacturer, model, commissioning dates, hierarchical sub-components via schema:hasPart, and domain-specific typing. Instruments may be standalone devices or complex systems with sub-components.

@id.description: Persistent identifier URI for this instrument metadata record.

@type.description: Must include schema:Product and schema:Thing. May include additional types.

schema:additionalType.description: Domain-specific type classifications. Should include a scientific instrument type URI (e.g. wd:Q3099911 for Wikidata scientific instrument).

schema:description.description: Text description of this instrument, its purpose, and capabilities.

schema:alternateName.description: Alternate name(s), e.g. specific make/model designation, common abbreviation.

schema:identifier.description: Formal identifier(s) for this instrument. Use PropertyValue for structured identifiers (e.g. PIDINST, serial number, inventory number).

schema:url.description: Landing page URL for this instrument.

schema:model.description: Product model information for this instrument.

schema:category.description: Instrument type classification(s) from a controlled vocabulary.

schema:contributor.description: Agents associated with this instrument in specific roles (e.g. operator, custodian, principal investigator). Use schema:owner for the owning organization.

schema:additionalProperty.description: Instrument-specific properties (measured variables, detection limits, calibration information, operating parameters, etc.). On a procedure / plan instrument (e.g. an instrument named directly on an ada:TAPPDefinition) these are schema:PropertyValueSpecification parameter templates (an overridable default); on a prov:used analysis-event instrument they are schema:PropertyValue concrete values. The JSON Schema accepts both; a profile SHACL rule pins which form applies in which context.

schema:validThrough.description: Date the instrument was decommissioned (ISO 8601). Absent if still operational.

schema:hasPart.description: Sub-components of this instrument system. Each item is either an inline instrument description or an @id reference.

@id.description: Reference to a sub-component defined elsewhere.

schema:relatedLink.description: Links to related resources (manuals, datasheets, calibration records, related instruments).

schema:subjectOf.description: Catalog record metadata-about-metadata for this instrument description.

schema:dateModified.description: Date this metadata record was last modified (ISO 8601).

dcterms:conformsTo.description: Schema or profile this metadata record conforms to.

@id.description: Identifier for this instrument within the record. REQUIRED: an instrument has to be referenceable. A monitored species names the instrument (or the instrument part) that reports it, and a dataset variable points back at the device that produced it; neither is expressible while the instrument is an anonymous object. A document-scoped identifier suffices, but a resolvable one is better wherever the lab has a persistent identifier for the device.

schema:additionalType.description: Domain-specific instrument type classifications. Should include a NeXus base class (e.g. nxs:base_classes/NXinstrument.html) and/or technique-specific identifier (e.g. ada:AMSInstrument, GCMD instrument identifier). URI-shape values MUST be serialized as JSON-LD IRI references ({"@id":"..."}); free-label strings remain valid. Every instrument additionally carries the Wikidata "measuring instrument" type, which is invariant across techniques: the technique-specific entry says what KIND of instrument this is and varies by profile, while the Wikidata term says that it is an instrument at all, and gives a consumer one term to select on without knowing the ADA vocabulary.

schema:hasPart.description: Sub-components of this instrument system (a torch, an ICP source, a collision/reaction cell, a spectrometer). A component IS an instrument -- same @type (schema:Product + schema:Thing), same Wikidata term, and its own schema:additionalType token saying which kind of component it is. The shape is restated rather than written as `$ref: '#'`, because resolve_schema replaces a circular ref with an empty stub -- it would read as "a part is an instrument" and enforce nothing. Upstream types a component more loosely (schema:Thing alone, no Wikidata); this narrows it, and the two compose because allOf intersects.

@id.description: Identifier for this component within the record. REQUIRED on an INLINE component for the same reason it is required on the instrument: a monitored species names the part that reports it -- a Faraday cup, a spectrometer, a detector -- and an anonymous object cannot be referenced. The sibling branch of this anyOf is the by-reference form, a bare {"@id": ...} pointing at a component described elsewhere.

anyOf.description: Reference by node @id to a component described elsewhere.

ProcedureIdentification.title: ICPMS on the procedure
ProcedureIdentification.description: Composed into a TAPP (prov:Plan) schema: what the procedure asserts once, for every analysis that follows it.

ada:ionCounterDeadTimeDefault.description: Dead time of each ion-counting detector channel, used in the dead-time correction applied to high count rates. Distinct from pulse/analog cross-calibration, which relates the two detector modes rather than correcting counting losses within the pulse-counting mode.

ada:uncertaintyLevel.description: The convention at which reported uncertainties are quoted — 1-sigma, 2-sigma, or a 95% confidence interval — and whether a measured spread is reported as a standard error or a standard deviation. State the convention applying to all values reported under this procedure, and state each separately where different reported quantities use different conventions. Distinct from Uncertainty Propagation Method, which addresses how component uncertainties are combined rather than how the result is quoted.

schema:name.description: Type of plasma torch installed (e.g. standard quartz, high-matrix, low-flow).

ada:calibrationMeasurementFrequency.description: How often the primary calibration or bracketing standard is measured relative to unknown samples within a session. Specify the bracketing scheme where a fixed one is used, such as one standard measurement before and after each sample.

ada:oxideProductionMethodAndThreshold.description: Method used to quantify plasma oxide production and the acceptance threshold applied before commencing analysis. Record both the monitored mass ratio(s) and the maximum allowed threshold(s). Measured values are recorded in Oxide Production. The monitored ratio is procedure-dependent: ThO+/Th+ (m/z 248/232), UO+/U+ (254/238), CeO+/Ce+ (156/140) and BaO+/Ba+ are all in use.

ada:blankBackgroundCorrectionMethod.description: Method used to subtract background and, where relevant, procedural blank from the measured signal. State what is subtracted - instrument background acquired with no sample reaching the plasma, an on-peak zero acquired on the same matrix, or a separately measured procedural blank - over what interval it is measured, and at what granularity it is applied.

ada:internalStandardElement.description: Element(s) used as the internal standard, the monitored isotope, and how the internal-standard concentration was established for unknowns. Where the element serves isotope-ratio work it must have a known isotopic composition and a mass close to the analyte's. Record 'None' together with the alternative used where no internal standard is applied.

items.description: Approach used to convert measured ion signals to reported concentrations, and specifically any case where different analytes or analyte groups within one procedure are calibrated differently - different primary standards for different mass ranges or phases, or one element serving as internal standard while others are externally calibrated. Where a single strategy applies to all analytes, record that strategy. Where the procedure reports isotope ratios only and no concentrations, record 'Not applicable (isotope ratios only)'.

ada:signalIntegrationIntervalMethod.description: Method used to define which portion of the acquired signal is integrated for each reported measurement, and the rule for excluding unstable or anomalous portions. State whether the interval is the full acquisition, a stable sub-interval selected by inspection, or selected by an automated criterion, and name the criterion.

ada:analysisSequenceDefault.description: The repeating order in which calibration or bracketing standards, quality-control and secondary reference materials, blanks and unknowns are interleaved within a measurement session. Adjustments must maintain the bracketing strategy defined in the procedure.

AnalysisIdentification.title: ICPMS on the analysis
AnalysisIdentification.description: Composed into a technique detail (schema:Dataset) schema: what each run supplies fresh, because it cannot be known until the analysis happens.

schema:identifier.description: Serial number or laboratory-internal identifier for the specific instrument unit.

ada:sensitivityYield.description: Instrument sensitivity achieved in the session, with the isotope or channel it was measured on and the conditions it applies to. May be expressed either as detected signal per unit concentration or per unit mass of analyte delivered — counts per second per ppb, volts per ppm, counts per picogram — or as useful yield, the percentage of sampled atoms ultimately detected as ions, with the method used to derive it cited. A sensitivity the procedure requires before analyses may begin belongs with the tuning acceptance criteria.

dqv:value.description: Measured oxide production ratio obtained during session-start tuning, for the proxy specified in Oxide Production Method and Threshold. Record the measured value and confirm whether the procedure threshold was met.

Param_Analysis_torchDepth.title: Torch Depth
Param_Analysis_torchDepth.description: Distance between the load coil and the sampling cone tip (mm), also called injector depth or torch position depending on the instrument manufacturer.

Param_Procedure_torchDepth.title: Torch Depth
Param_Procedure_torchDepth.description: Distance between the load coil and the sampling cone tip (mm), also called injector depth or torch position depending on the instrument manufacturer.

Param_Analysis_icpTuning.title: ICP Tuning
Param_Analysis_icpTuning.description: Description of the approach used to optimise ICP plasma conditions prior to analysis, including the reference material used for tuning and the acceptance criteria (e.g., oxide production threshold, sensitivity targets, mass calibration).

Param_Procedure_icpTuning.title: ICP Tuning
Param_Procedure_icpTuning.description: Description of the approach used to optimise ICP plasma conditions prior to analysis, including the reference material used for tuning and the acceptance criteria (e.g., oxide production threshold, sensitivity targets, mass calibration).

Param_Procedure_instrumentWarmUpSessionD.title: Instrument Warm up Session Duration Limit
Param_Procedure_instrumentWarmUpSessionD.description: Minimum warm-up time required after plasma ignition before analyses begin, and any maximum session duration enforced to maintain stable operating conditions.

schema:name.const: Instrument Warm up Session Duration Limit

Param_Analysis_makeUpGasAndFlowRate.title: Make-up Gas and Flow Rate
Param_Analysis_makeUpGasAndFlowRate.description: Supplementary gas added to the sample-carrying stream between the sample introduction system and the plasma, with its identity and the procedure-registered target flow rate. Record any small nitrogen or hydrogen addition with its own flow, whose unit commonly differs from the make-up flow. Record 'None' explicitly where no supplementary gas is added, to distinguish it from not reported.

Param_Procedure_makeUpGasAndFlowRate.title: Make-up Gas and Flow Rate
Param_Procedure_makeUpGasAndFlowRate.description: Supplementary gas added to the sample-carrying stream between the sample introduction system and the plasma, with its identity and the procedure-registered target flow rate. Record any small nitrogen or hydrogen addition with its own flow, whose unit commonly differs from the make-up flow. Record 'None' explicitly where no supplementary gas is added, to distinguish it from not reported.

Param_Analysis_ionCounterDeadTime.title: Ion Counter Dead Time
Param_Analysis_ionCounterDeadTime.description: Dead time of each ion-counting detector channel, used in the dead-time correction applied to high count rates. Distinct from pulse/analog cross-calibration, which relates the two detector modes rather than correcting counting losses within the pulse-counting mode.

Param_Analysis_uncertaintyPropagationMet.title: Uncertainty Propagation Method
Param_Analysis_uncertaintyPropagationMet.description: The approach used to propagate analytical uncertainty through the data reduction chain to the final reported value. State which sources are included in the propagation: counting statistics, calibration standard uncertainty, internal standard uncertainty, drift correction, and any systematic contributions. Distinct from Uncertainty Level, which states the convention at which the resulting uncertainty is quoted.

Param_Procedure_uncertaintyPropagationMe.title: Uncertainty Propagation Method
Param_Procedure_uncertaintyPropagationMe.description: The approach used to propagate analytical uncertainty through the data reduction chain to the final reported value. State which sources are included in the propagation: counting statistics, calibration standard uncertainty, internal standard uncertainty, drift correction, and any systematic contributions. Distinct from Uncertainty Level, which states the convention at which the resulting uncertainty is quoted.

Param_Analysis_auxiliaryGasFlowRate.title: Auxiliary Gas Flow Rate
Param_Analysis_auxiliaryGasFlowRate.description: Flow rate of the intermediate (auxiliary) argon gas stream, between the torch body and the injector tube, which positions the plasma relative to the load coil, in L/min. Distinct from the outer coolant (plasma) gas and from the gas stream that carries sample into the plasma.

Param_Procedure_auxiliaryGasFlowRate.title: Auxiliary Gas Flow Rate
Param_Procedure_auxiliaryGasFlowRate.description: Flow rate of the intermediate (auxiliary) argon gas stream, between the torch body and the injector tube, which positions the plasma relative to the load coil, in L/min. Distinct from the outer coolant (plasma) gas and from the gas stream that carries sample into the plasma.

Param_Analysis_coolantPlasmaGasFlowRate.title: Coolant Plasma Gas Flow Rate
Param_Analysis_coolantPlasmaGasFlowRate.description: Flow rate of the outer (coolant/plasma) argon gas stream that sustains the ICP plasma, in L/min.

Param_Procedure_coolantPlasmaGasFlowRate.title: Coolant Plasma Gas Flow Rate
Param_Procedure_coolantPlasmaGasFlowRate.description: Flow rate of the outer (coolant/plasma) argon gas stream that sustains the ICP plasma, in L/min.

Param_Analysis_rfPower.title: RF Power
Param_Analysis_rfPower.description: Radiofrequency forward power applied to the ICP, in watts.

Param_Procedure_rfPower.title: RF Power
Param_Procedure_rfPower.description: Radiofrequency forward power applied to the ICP, in watts.

Param_Procedure_guardElectrode.title: Guard Electrode
Param_Procedure_guardElectrode.description: Whether a guard electrode - also called a grounded shield electrode, extraction lens, or Fassel torch shield - is installed and active on the torch assembly.

Param_Procedure_plasmaThermalMode.title: Plasma Thermal Mode
Param_Procedure_plasmaThermalMode.description: Whether the ICP plasma is operated under cool plasma (<=900 W RF) or normal (hot) plasma (>1000 W RF) conditions, with the RF power that defines it. This field records the RF-POWER axis only. Solvent loading also affects plasma thermal state, but dry versus wet aerosol is recorded by Desolvation System — do not answer this field with 'dry plasma' or 'wet plasma'. Document independently of the RF Power field.

Param_Analysis_filteringApproach.title: Filtering Approach
Param_Analysis_filteringApproach.description: Criteria used to identify and exclude anomalous data - signal spikes, individual cycles, or whole replicate measurements - before the reported value is calculated. State where in the reduction sequence the filter is applied.

Param_Procedure_filteringApproach.title: Filtering Approach
Param_Procedure_filteringApproach.description: Criteria used to identify and exclude anomalous data - signal spikes, individual cycles, or whole replicate measurements - before the reported value is calculated. State where in the reduction sequence the filter is applied.

Param_Procedure_configuration.title: Configuration
Param_Procedure_configuration.description: Geometry and designation of the sampler and skimmer cones installed during analysis. State both cones.

Param_Analysis_signalIntegrationTime.title: Signal Integration Time
Param_Analysis_signalIntegrationTime.description: The integration time actually used for the reported signal, in seconds - the time retained after the signal-integration interval has been applied, and therefore equal to or shorter than the total acquisition. Where the procedure computes it from an acquisition structure, record that basis.

Param_Analysis_memoryEffectMitigation.title: Memory Effect Mitigation
Param_Analysis_memoryEffectMitigation.description: Procedure applied to identify and minimise carry-over of high-concentration or isotopically distinct material from a preceding measurement into the current one. Mitigation is applied primarily at measurement time, by allowing sufficient washout or rinse between successive introductions. At data processing level, record any flagging or exclusion of measurements where the required washout may not have been achieved.

Param_Procedure_memoryEffectMitigation.title: Memory Effect Mitigation
Param_Procedure_memoryEffectMitigation.description: Procedure applied to identify and minimise carry-over of high-concentration or isotopically distinct material from a preceding measurement into the current one. Mitigation is applied primarily at measurement time, by allowing sufficient washout or rinse between successive introductions. At data processing level, record any flagging or exclusion of measurements where the required washout may not have been achieved.

Param_Procedure_isotopeDilutionDataReduc.title: Isotope Dilution Data Reduction Method
Param_Procedure_isotopeDilutionDataReduc.description: Mass balance approach used to calculate sample mass fractions, and where applicable isotope ratios, from spike-sample isotope ratio measurements. For double-spike procedures the ratios and concentrations are co-determined through the spike inversion; for conventional isotope dilution the IUPAC ID equations are used. Record 'None' where neither isotope dilution nor double-spike methods are applied.

Param_Analysis_massResolutionSetting.title: Mass Resolution Setting
Param_Analysis_massResolutionSetting.description: Operating mass resolution of the mass analyser. Where the analyser permits selection, state the mode; where individual analytes are assigned to different modes, state each.

Param_Procedure_massResolutionSetting.title: Mass Resolution Setting
Param_Procedure_massResolutionSetting.description: Operating mass resolution of the mass analyser. Where the analyser permits selection, state the mode; where individual analytes are assigned to different modes, state each.

Param_Procedure_samplerAndSkimmerConeMat.title: Sampler and Skimmer Cone Material
Param_Procedure_samplerAndSkimmerConeMat.description: Material composition of the sampler and skimmer cones. State both sampler and skimmer materials; a single statement is acceptable where they are identical.

Param_Analysis_analysisSequence.title: Analysis Sequence
Param_Analysis_analysisSequence.description: The repeating order in which calibration or bracketing standards, quality-control and secondary reference materials, blanks and unknowns are interleaved within a measurement session. Adjustments must maintain the bracketing strategy defined in the procedure.

Identifier.description:
Properties for a schema.org identifier (schema:PropertyValue pattern).
**Union-type policy:** In CDIF profile UML models an attribute typed as
schema:Identifier / schema:PropertyValue is represented by a single attribute
of that class type. The JSON Schema implementation permits the property value
to be EITHER a plain string (interpreted as the bare identifier value) OR a
full schema:PropertyValue object (with explicit @type, propertyID, value).
Consumers should accept either form.

schema:propertyID.description: In this context for the schema:PropertyValue, this field is an identifier for the identifier schema, e.g. DOI, ARK.  Get values from https://registry.identifiers.org/registry/ for interoperability. URI-shape values MUST be serialized as JSON-LD IRI references ({"@id":"..."}) so they participate in RDF entailment; free-label strings remain valid as strings.

schema:url.description: web-resolveable string for the identifier; host name part is location of a resolver that will return some representation for the given identifier value. E.g. https://doi.org/10.5066/F7VX0DMQ

schema:name.description: string label for organization that is meaningful for human users

schema:alternateName.description: other labels by which the organization might be known

DefinedTerm.description:
schema.org Defined Term schema.

**Union-type policy:** In CDIF profile UML models an attribute typed as
schema:DefinedTerm is represented by a single attribute of that class type.
The JSON Schema implementation permits the property value to be EITHER a
plain string (interpreted as schema:name or schema:termCode in the default
vocabulary) OR a full schema:DefinedTerm object (with explicit @type, name,
identifier, termCode, inDefinedTermSet). Consumers should accept either form.

Note that this differs from the cdif Concept policy: a Concept (skos:Concept)
in CDIF profiles MUST be a controlled-vocabulary entry (object form or
@id-reference) — plain strings are not permitted for Concept-typed values
because vocabulary identity cannot be recovered from an unscoped label.

AdditionalProperty.title: additionalProperty PropertyValue
AdditionalProperty.description: PropertyValue values required to define a soft-typed property with a value.

schema:propertyID.description: identifier or name for the property concept quantified by the values in this variable slot. Multiple values can specify the property at different levels of granularity.

AdditionalPropertySpecification.title: additionalProperty PropertyValueSpecification
AdditionalPropertySpecification.description: A parameter specification (an overridable default) declared on a procedure / plan instrument, typed schema:PropertyValueSpecification; the default sits in schema:defaultValue. Contrast with AdditionalProperty (schema:PropertyValue), the concrete-value form carried by a prov:used analysis-event instrument.

InstrumentComponent.description: A sub-component of an instrument system. Uses the same structure as the parent instrument but without nesting (single level of hasPart).

Reference.description: Building block to implement relations to other resources using a URL and some semantics.

allOf.description: schema for a labeled link, a profile of schema.org/CreativeWork

skos:prefLabel.description: Preferred lexical label for this concept. A single string, a single language-tagged value, or an array of language-tagged values. Each language should appear at most once.

skos:notation.description: Classification code for this concept within a scheme (a single notation string, consistent with CdifCodelistConcept).

skos:definition.description: Formal explanation of the meaning of this concept.

skos:inScheme.description: Concept scheme(s) this concept belongs to.

skos:broader.description: Broader (parent) concepts in the hierarchy. Items are inline concept objects or @id references.

skos:narrower.description: Narrower (child) concepts in the hierarchy. Items are inline concept objects or @id references.
